messages:
maya: Anyone else seeing canary failures in eu-west during the release? smoke tests show DB auth errors, but manifests didn't change. :rotating_light:
liam: Which pipeline/release?
maya: gitops-helm-release-v2, canary set 10%. Error is `ERROR auth: invalid credentials` from app logs. No recent DB rotation.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: helm release gitops-helm-release-v2 #452 reported 502s from smoke-checker in eu-west (canary) 2065432105
sonia: I pulled sops-agent logs from the pre-render sidecar on the canary render pod, looks like decrypt returned old creds:
```
2026-03-20T09:15:02Z sops-agent INFO cache hit key=env/db-creds
2026-03-20T09:15:02Z sops-agent INFO returning cached payload sha=7f4a9b
2026-03-20T09:15:03Z kms ERROR ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
```
maya: but git shows secret updated in repo 2 hours ago, and the canary used the new commit. Why would cache return old payload?
ken: hypothesis: the sops pre-renderer caches decrypted blobs on the agent host at /var/sops-cache keyed by secret name only. Our gitops overlay flips namespaces during canary and reuses the same secret name which makes cache collisions possible across clusters when the agent is reused during bursty deploys.
liam: oh, we did a bursty rollout earlier today (20 parallel helm renders) to reduce latency, maybe agent restarted mid-burst and kept cache dir mounted between pods. Can we confirm cache keys?
sonia: confirmed. agent config shows `cache_key_template: "{name}"` and TTL 24h. So no commit or namespace context. Plus KMS throttling caused some decrypts to fail so agent fell back to cache.
jen: ugh. So combination = old cached secret + KMS throttling = stale creds injected into canary pods.
ken: short-term fix: force-purge cache on all pre-renderers and throttle parallelism in the release job. Run a k8s job: `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/sops-pre-renderer -- rm -rf /var/sops-cache/*`
maya: ran the purge on eu-west pre-renderers, restarted renderer pods. Smoke tests are green for 8/10 canaries now, two still getting auth errors.
liam: which two?
maya: eu-west-1b and eu-west-1c, same cluster but different node pools. Logs show KMS throttling spiking during the burst: `ThrottlingException` followed by quick cache hit fallback.
sonia: medium-term fix suggestions: change cache key to include `repo_commit` and `namespace` and add stronger backoff + jitter for KMS calls. Also reduce default concurrency in helm pipeline from 20 -> 4.
ken: agree. Also we should make cache TTL short (e.g., 5m) for pre-render stage or invalidate cache on a new git commit id.
jen: for rollout automation: add a post-render hook to helm pipeline that triggers `sops-agent invalidate --commit $GIT_COMMIT` or simply run `sops --decrypt` in the CI runner with the commit context and avoid relying on shared agent cache for renders. That keeps each release hermetic.
liam: I can push a quick pipeline change to limit parallel renders and add a one-off job to invalidate caches in all regions. Then follow up with a config change to cache key and TTL.
maya: please do. Also let's add a smoke-check gating step to fail fast if auth errors > 1%.
sonia: I'll prepare the agent PR (0.9.3) that includes the cache-key fix and exponential backoff for KMS (with jitter).
ken: ops follow-up: create k8s Job manifests to purge cache and add to runbooks.
deploy-bot: action created: #INFRA-623 purge sops-cache across regions, assignee liam, due EOD
liam: doing the purge now across eu-west and us-central. updating concurrency and adding smoke gate.
maya: after purge and throttling reduction smoke is green in eu-west. Rolling canary back to 30% to verify. :thumbsup:
jen: long-term: consider moving decrypt step into the build artifact stage so runtime agents aren't a single point of staleness.
maya: agreed. Action items recap: 1) purge caches (liam) 2) throttle parallel renders (liam) 3) agent PR for cache key + TTL + backoff (sonia) 4) add commit-based invalidation or CI-side decrypt (jen) 5) add smoke auth gating to pipeline (maya)
ken: I'll update the runbook and add the `rm -rf` job template.
sonia: creating PR now, will link to INFRA-623.
maya: thanks team, will monitor canary and mark incident closed once canary stays healthy for 1h.
